hints.title: Greedy Highest Frequency Selection
hints.text: Always schedule the available character with the greatest remaining count that has satisfied the separation constraint.

hints.title: Buffer Cooldown Delay
hints.text: After placing a character, place it into a waiting line so that it cannot be selected again until k steps have elapsed.

hints.title: Max Frequency Heap with FIFO Cooldown
hints.text: Count frequencies into a max-heap. Pop the highest count character, decrement count, and push to a cooldown queue. When queue length reaches k, release cooled characters back to heap.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def rearrangeString(self, s: str, k: int) -> str:
        if k <= 1:
            return s
        from collections import Counter, deque
        import heapq
        counts = Counter(s)
        max_heap = [(-cnt, ch) for ch, cnt in counts.items()]
        heapq.heapify(max_heap)
        cooldown = deque()
        res = []
        while max_heap:
            cnt, ch = heapq.heappop(max_heap)
            res.append(ch)
            cooldown.append((cnt + 1, ch))
            if len(cooldown) >= k:
                ready_cnt, ready_ch = cooldown.popleft()
                if ready_cnt < 0:
                    heapq.heappush(max_heap, (ready_cnt, ready_ch))
        return "".join(res) if len(res) == len(s) else ""
```

complexity.notes: Optimal greedy solution running in O(N log A) time and O(A) auxiliary space bounded by alphabet size.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Arbitrary placement quickly creates unavoidable adjacent traps with leftover frequent letters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Max-heap prioritizes urgent characters while cooldown queue enforces minimum k separation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle edge cases k = 0 or k = 1 and detect impossible configurations when result length < s length.
